1: Registry composition by kind. 224 catalogue records: 81 model, 59 software, 23 benchmark, 22 database, 14 dataset, 10 agent, 7 tutorial, 4 paper, 3 standard, 1 model asset. A count of records says nothing about whether a record has been verified, and the figure carries no status, access or openness information.
10: Acquisition policies on two retrospective assay replays, on CHEMBL5736995, 124 compounds were acquired against a pool of 631, and the diversity policy recovered 0.0508 of the top decile against 0.1133 for the ensemble-variance policy and on CHEMBL3705421, 24 compounds were acquired against a pool of 130, and the diversity policy recovered 0.0000 of the top decile against 0.1635 for the ensemble-variance policy. The two named policies are drawn in colour and the five random policy instances in one colour with a distinct marker each, because they are five fixed seeds of one policy rather than five methods. These are retrospective replays and not prospective experiments, the random seeds are not independent replicates, and no confidence intervals or p values are reported.
11: The uncertainty of a trajectory observable, from the rMD17 lab page. Ethanol has a naive standard error of 0.000087 Å against a block-averaged standard error of 0.000288 Å at 100 blocks and Malonaldehyde has a naive standard error of 0.000235 Å against a block-averaged standard error of 0.001472 Å at 100 blocks. The middle panel is the ratio between the two estimates, which is the number the page reports. The right is ethanol's block-averaged standard error against the block count, because a corrected estimate still carries a choice inside it. There is one trajectory per molecule and one level of theory, so nothing here speaks to replicate dependence or force-field sensitivity.
12: The cumulative mean of the radius of gyration against the full 100,000-frame mean, from the rMD17 lab page. +0.00198 Å for ethanol and -0.02528 Å for malonaldehyde at 100 frames, +0.00254 Å for ethanol and -0.00743 Å for malonaldehyde at 1,000 frames and +0.00054 Å for ethanol and -0.00946 Å for malonaldehyde at 10,000 frames. The malonaldehyde curve is not monotone, being closer at a thousand frames than at ten thousand, and that is drawn as the data stands. One trajectory per molecule and one level of theory means nothing here speaks to replicate dependence or force-field sensitivity.
13: Two pairs of assay systems that disagree. CYP2D6 against CYP3A4, all pairs reaches a Pearson r of 0.2987 and a Spearman rho of 0.2981 over 1195 shared molecules, CYP2D6 against CYP3A4, clean pairs reaches a Pearson r of 0.2990 and a Spearman rho of 0.3038 over 1015 shared molecules, microsome against rat hepatocyte reaches a Pearson r of 0.3410 and a Spearman rho of 0.3868 over 359 shared molecules, microsome against human hepatocyte reaches a Pearson r of 0.4083 and a Spearman rho of 0.4864 over 96 shared molecules and human hepatocyte against rat hepatocyte reaches a Pearson r of 0.3095 and a Spearman rho of 0.4732 over 106 shared molecules. The six largest disagreements between the two CYP systems span 2.46 to 2.90 pChEMBL in both directions, with the first system higher on three molecules and the second on three. A correlation near 0.3 means a measurement in one system carries little information about the other, which is not the same as saying either system is wrong, and the six molecules are the extremes the review found rather than a sample of the distribution.
2: Coverage bounds for thirteen providers across five thresholds, each bound a lower and an upper count out of 93 topics. AIDD Commons is the first row and its bounds are equal at every threshold, 93 explained, 93 worked, 81 executable, 62 executable on real data and 81 assessed, because all 93 of its cells are direct observations. Every external row is an interval, because unobserved cells contribute to an upper bound and nothing to a lower one. The bounds are not confidence intervals and no probability attaches to them.
3: Curriculum units per track across the 18 tracks, split by layer, beside the number of lessons in each track. The curriculum holds 120 learning units in 127 lessons, 56 core, 44 research and 20 practice. A unit is a learning objective attached to a lesson, so the two counts differ, and neither one says how long a track takes or whether a learner reaches its end.
4: Observed depth per track for this project's 93 audited topics, beside the basis each track's runnable topics rest on. 12 worked, 0 executable and 81 assessed, and of the 81 runnable topics 62 rest on real data and 19 rest on authored inputs. Depth records what a reviewer observed in the material, not what a learner achieved.
5: This project's own record against a blind second reading of the same 93 topics by a reviewer from a different model family on 2026-09-11. The reading agreed with the record on 93 topics, read 0 deeper and 0 shallower. At the thresholds the reading gave 93 explained, 93 worked, 81 executable, 62 executable on real data and 81 assessed against the recorded 93 explained, 93 worked, 81 executable, 62 executable on real data and 81 assessed. The reviewer had also written parts of the course, so this is a second reading and not a blind replication.
6: Openness by record kind and by the seven openness dimensions, over 224 catalogue records. The fill is the share of a kind's records for which a dimension is available, counted over the records for which it applies, and the hatch says why the rest is not available, unverified, recorded as not available, or not applicable to that kind. Openness is recorded per dimension and is never collapsed here into a single open or closed label.
7: Access level and licence layer for the 224 catalogue records. 4 records carry no verified access level and 18 record no licence. The verified access levels are 1 open weights, 160 open source, 41 source available, 6 research only, 10 gated, 2 closed. By licence layer, 8 public domain dedication, 123 permissive software licence, 30 creative commons attribution, 23 copyleft, 7 creative commons non-commercial, 15 other stated terms. A record with more than one licence is counted once, in the most restrictive layer it carries.
8: FreeSolv point and interval metrics for two fixed teaching baselines, on the predeclared scaffold split and the easier random split. The ridge reaches 1.13 kcal/mol mean absolute error on the scaffold split against 2.59 for the training-set mean, and 1.02 against 2.77 on the random split. On the scaffold split the intervals reach an empirical coverage of 0.875 for the ridge and 0.90625 for the forest, at mean widths of 5.48 and 6.01 kcal/mol. The coverage is marginal coverage and not conditional calibration, the nominal level of the intervals is not stated in the reviewed results, and these teaching baselines establish no state of the art.
9: The same three baselines on the primary partition of 132 compounds and on the separate assay replication of 170 compounds. The Morgan ridge is the best of the three on the primary partition at 0.418 mean absolute error, while the descriptor ridge is the best on the replication at 0.579; the Morgan ridge reaches 3.132 there and its rank correlation falls from 0.505 to -0.041. The two evaluations are separate comparisons and success on one does not erase failure on the other, the acquisition lab had accessed labels shared with this evaluation before it ran, and no confidence intervals or p values are reported.
